extra.text: "Another one off the coast road? Garran. This is my forge, such as it is. No ore's come up the road in months, and the forge has been cold since."
"Quarry's up the hill path, past the stream. Rusty seams in the rock face. Three good lumps."
"Iron's ready. Knife, buckler or gloves. Doesn't matter which. Matters that you make it yourself."
"Forge is hot. Iron's sixty coppers a bar. Anything you make, you keep."

choices.label: "Is there any work?"
choices.result: Garran looks at your hands, then at the cold forge. "Work's the one thing I've plenty of. Ore's the thing I haven't." He hands you a pick with a new handle on an old head. "There's a quarry up in the hills, past the stream. Old seams in the rock face, rusty red. Bring me three good lumps and I'll show you what to do with them."

choices.label: "I've got the ore."
choices.result: Garran weighs each lump in his palm and grunts. He takes his pick back first. Then he banks the furnace and feeds it the ore, and an hour later there's a rough bar of iron cooling on the bench. "Yours. Now make something of it."

choices.label: "I found this at the quarry."
choices.result: Garran turns the green stone to the light. "Green glass, the old quarrymen called it. They'd pocket it and never say." He drops it back in your hand. "It's worth more to you set in something than to me in a drawer. Use it."

choices.result: Garran shows you how, once, then hands you the tongs. "Your turn."

scenes.title: The well
text: The village well. The rope's new, which is more than you can say for anything else here.

extra.text: Ida said not the well: folk need it. Stream water, from up the hill.

choices.label: Drink and fill your waterskin
choices.result: The well water tastes of stone. You drink your fill and top up the skin.

extra.text: "You're the one Yenson pulled out of the sea? Ida. I keep the hunters' lodge, what's left of it. Three of us, and a larder you could dance in."
"Snares are up in the hills, west of the path. Rook's out there, he'll show you. Wood's by the block. Water from the hill stream, mind, not the well. Folk need the well."
"Larder's full for once. But there's something else, and it's been eating at me."
"The den's past the quarry, up in the north-east corner of the hills. Keep Rook fed and behind you. Bring him back."
"Go and see the others, if you haven't. Garran at the forge. Old Orlen up the hill. They could all use a hand."
Ida doesn't quite look at you. There's a bow hung over the lodge door that wasn't there before.

choices.label: "Any work going?"
choices.result: Ida looks you up and down. "Food, wood, water. Same as every day, and there's not enough of us to do it." She counts on her fingers. "Rook's snares want checking, up in the hills: three hares. Four logs split at the block. And the water butt's dry. Fill a pail at the hill stream and tip it in." She shoves a pail at you. "Do that and you've earned your supper."

choices.label: "What happened to Skelmed?"
choices.result: "The levy happened. Half of every catch to the crown, and the collector takes his own bite on top. The young ones went inland. The merchants stopped coming when the roads went bad." She spits. "Wolves on the coast road. Wolves. In my grandmother's day you'd never see one this side of the hills."

choices.label: "Anything else?"
choices.result: "The wolves. There's a big one leading them now: grey, scar across its muzzle, denning past the quarry. Kill it and the rest will scatter." She whistles, and Rook comes round the lodge with two bows. He hands you the older one. "He goes with you. He knows the hills." She pushes a fish, two rolls of linen and a flask of spirits into your arms. "Feed him first. And clean any bite before you bind it."

choices.label: "The pack leader's dead."
choices.result: Ida looks at the pelt, then at Rook, then at you, and lets out a breath she seems to have been holding for a month. "Good." She presses two silver on you, and this time she won't hear a word about it. Rook clears his throat. "I've business in the town inland. Pelts to sell, and a man there who owes the lodge money." He shrugs his bow higher on his shoulder. "Roads are bad. I'll walk with you as far as the town, if you're going. After that you're on your own."

choices.label: "The pack leader's dead. Rook isn't coming back."
choices.result: Ida takes the pelt without looking at it. For a long time she doesn't say anything at all. "He was nineteen," she says at last. She puts two silver in your hand and closes your fingers over them, and goes inside, and shuts the door.

choices.label: "What now?"
choices.result: Ida's quiet for a while. "You've done right by us. But a few odd jobs won't mend this place. Everything that's wrong here comes down the road from the town inland: the collector, the levy, the soldiers who won't clear the roads." She looks you up and down. "Somebody ought to go and see. Somebody who can handle themselves."

scenes.speaker: Ida
scenes.title: Payment
text: Ida counts a silver's worth of coppers into her palm, slowly, the way people count money they can't spare. She holds them out to you, with two parcels of smoked fish.

choices.label: Take it and thank her
choices.result: "Earned it," says Ida, and that's the end of it.

choices.label: Take the fish, leave the coin. She needs it more
choices.result: Ida looks at you a long moment, then puts the coins away without a word. Later you hear her telling Bess about it, twice.

choices.label: Tell her it was worth more than a silver
choices.result: Ida's mouth goes thin. She finds another sixty coppers from somewhere and puts them in your hand, hard. "There. Don't spend it all at once."

scenes.title: The chopping block
text: The lodge's chopping block, an axe bitten into it, and a heap of rounds waiting beside it.

extra.text: That's four split. Enough for Ida.

choices.label: Split a log
choices.result: Set it, swing, and the round splits clean with a crack that echoes off the houses.

scenes.title: The water butt
text: The lodge's water butt, a barrel as tall as your chest.

choices.label: Pour in the pail
choices.result: The water goes in with a heavy slosh. That'll do Ida for a few days.

scenes.title: The fire's out
text: The last flames hiss out. The net shed is black and steaming, but it's standing, and the boats are untouched. People who've watched you for days from behind their shutters come out to stare.
"Lesson two," says Orlen, out of breath and leaning on his stick. "Fire's easy. Anyone can start one. Putting it out, that's the magic."

extra.text: A dockhand is staring at your hands. "You pulled that water out of nothing," he says. By tonight, everyone in Skelmed will have heard it.
"Bed, bread or bandages? I've all three, and potions for the bad days."
"Saw what you did at the net shed. Most anyone's done for this village in a year. What can I get you?"
Beds are thirty coppers. Sleeping saves your game.

choices.needText: A bed's 30 coppers, and you haven't got them.

choices.label: Buy a loaf of bread (6 coppers)
choices.needText: You haven't six coppers to your name.
choices.result: Bess wraps a loaf in a cloth. "Yesterday's. Still good."

choices.label: Buy a bandage (15 coppers)
choices.result: Bess fetches a roll of clean linen from a chest. "For the cuts. There's always cuts."

choices.label: Buy a flask of spirits (30 coppers)
choices.result: "Don't drink it all at once. Or at all, really. It's for wounds."

choices.label: Buy willow bark (10 coppers)
choices.result: "For fevers. Brew it, it's foul. Or there's a willow up by the hill stream, if you'd rather pick your own."

choices.label: Buy a health potion (40 coppers)
choices.result: "Orlen brews them. Tastes like rust, works like a charm. Keep one back for the bad days."

choices.label: Buy a sewing kit (80 coppers)
choices.result: "Needle and good thread. Stitched up my husband with that, twice."

scenes.speaker: Dockhand
scenes.title: A dockhand
text: "Crabs come up on the sand south of the pier. Mind the claws, but the meat's worth it, if you've a knife."

scenes.speaker: Bess
scenes.title: You're bleeding
text: A broad woman in an apron is sweeping the step of the inn. She takes one look at the blood on you and drops the broom.

"Wolf? Thought so. Sit down before you fall down." She's back in a moment with a flask, a roll of linen and two little red bottles. "Bites go bad if you leave them. Clean it first, then bind it. Spirits for the cleaning, mind, not for drinking."
"The red ones are health potions. Drink one when you're badly hurt, or give one to a friend. They heal, they don't raise the dead, so don't wait too long. I sell them, when you've the coin."
"Go on, you do it. You'll be doing it yourself on the road, with no one to help."
